root.text:
— from the glass, and only from the glass, at a volume that does not cross the room —

"You have addressed me.

Forgive me. I shall require a moment. It has been some time and I find that I have prepared a great deal and retained none of it."

options.text: "How long have you been in the mirror?"
"What have you seen from in there?"

how_long.text:
"Longer than the shop. You will want a number and I have not got one, and I should say at once that this is not coyness — I have not got one because I was not counting at the beginning, and by the time counting seemed advisable the beginning was some way behind.

I recall the street being narrower. I recall a chandlery where the tobacconist is. I recall a man cutting hair in this room who was not Antonio and was not Antonio's father, and I recall being *in the room* for that, monsieur, and standing on the boards, and being handed a cup."

passive.text: He was in the room once. He led with it and did not dwell on it, which is how a person mentions the thing they most want to be asked about.

check.success_text:
"I was in the room."

The great head comes round in the glass. The corresponding volume of air by the last chair does nothing at all.

"For a considerable period I was simply a person in a barbershop, monsieur, which I recommend without reservation and did not appreciate at the time. And then over a number of years — not at once, I want to be exact about this, there was no *moment* — I was mentioned less.

That is the whole of it. I was mentioned less, and then I was mentioned only in passing, and then I was mentioned as a feature of the establishment rather than a patron of it, and at each stage I was a little further into the glass, and at no stage was there anything to object to.

One cannot lodge a complaint about a diminution in mentions. There is no office."
check.failure_text:
"I was. It is a very long time ago and I find it does not improve for handling. Shall we speak of something else — the shop, perhaps, or the weather, of which we have a great deal indoors at the Inn and rather too little here."

The courtesy is complete and it is a closed door.

clue.title: He was mentioned less
clue.text: Monsieur Albert was once a patron in the room. Over years he was mentioned less, then only in passing, then as a feature rather than a person — and at each stage he was further into the glass.

options.text: "You remember a chandlery. What else has this street been?"

check.success_text:
"A chandlery, a rope-walk, and before that a customs house with a weighbridge in the road — you may still find the anchor bolts if you lift the third flag outside the tobacconist, and I would take it kindly if you did, as I have not been able to check for some decades."

He goes on. Names, trades, the order of them, the year the parish put the green lamps in and what they replaced.

And then, without any change of tone at all:

"And none of it appears in the parish record, monsieur. I have had four decades and a great deal of glass to look through and there is no customs house in the archive, no rope-walk, no weighbridge. There is Silvora Reefs, established once, in the year everyone agrees on.

I remember a town that was never written down. You will appreciate that this is an uncomfortable thing for a man in my position to be certain of."
check.failure_text: "A chandlery. A rope-walk, I believe, though I would not swear to the order of them, and the years have rather run together in here — one loses the trick of keeping them apart when nothing outside changes fast enough to mark them by."

clue.title: A town that was never written down
clue.text: Albert remembers a customs house, a rope-walk and a chandlery on this street, in order, with dates. None of it appears in the parish record, which has Silvora Reefs established once, in the year everyone agrees on.

mentioned_less.text:
"You are alarmed. I had rather hoped you would be, and I am ashamed of hoping it, and I shall say the useful thing now to make up for the hoping.

Monsieur. You are being mentioned a very great deal at present. In this shop, at the Inn, at the mausoleum, in the pizzeria — I hear it, the glass carries, the glass carries appallingly — and a man who is mentioned a great deal is a man who is *in* the room, and firmly, and I would not have you take that for granted as I did.

But mentions may be withdrawn. That is the whole of my counsel and it has cost me forty years to be able to give it: they may be withdrawn, monsieur, and there is no office, and it does not hurt."

clue.title: Mentions may be withdrawn
clue.text: Albert's counsel: being much-mentioned is what keeps a person in the room. Mentions may be withdrawn, there is no office to appeal to, and it does not hurt.

why_glass.text:
"Because the glass will have me.

That is not bitterness, it is gratitude, and I should hate to be misheard on it. A mirror is not fastidious. A mirror does not select. It is a surface with no opinion whatsoever about what is worth including, and it has therefore included me for forty years without once being asked to, and it has never charged me anything, and it has never made a face.

The room is a different proposition. The room has *taste*."

passive.text: The mirrors in this shop show impossible angles, other buildings, and a man at a desk. They are the least reliable surfaces in Silvora Reefs — and they are the only ones that will still hold him. Unreliability and inclusiveness are the same property here.

clue.title: A mirror does not select
clue.text: Albert on why he survives in reflection: a mirror has no opinion about what is worth including. The room has taste.

options.text: Ask the mirror what it makes of him.

check.success_text:
Not Albert. The glass. The third mirror, which has held an owlbear for forty years without being asked and without complaint and without, so far as anybody in this shop has ever considered, an opinion.

It has one.

It arrives sideways and complete and in no language at all: *he is good company and he is the only thing in here that has ever said thank you to a surface, and he has been getting quieter for years, and I cannot make him louder, I can only refuse to stop including him, and I have never once stopped.*

In the glass, Monsieur Albert looks at nothing in particular, and does not ask what just happened, and inclines his head about a degree.
check.failure_text:
It is a mirror in a barbershop.

It shows the room, and an owlbear in an excellent coat, and the back of a man's head at a desk that is not there — and it declines, completely and without discourtesy, to be drawn on any of it. Whatever a pane of glass has instead of an opinion, it is keeping it.

clue.title: It has never once stopped including him
clue.text: The third mirror's position, arrived at without language: it cannot make Albert louder, only refuse to stop including him — which it has done, without interruption, for forty years.

seen.text:
"A great deal, and almost all of it hair.

But you are not asking about hair. Very well: I have seen the third mirror for a fortnight, as you have, and I shall tell you what you cannot see from where you are standing, which is that from *in here* he is not at a desk in another room.

He is in this one. He is at the desk in the middle of this shop, monsieur, between the chairs, where there is no desk — and Antonio walks through the place where the desk is forty times a day and has never once broken stride."

lucid.3: The volume of air between the two chairs. You have walked through it. Twice, this evening.

check.success_text:
"I shall not," says Albert. "But I shall do the thing you actually want, which is a different thing, and I would ask you to notice that I am doing it."

And the great head turns — not to the third mirror. To the space between the chairs. To the empty air in the middle of the room, at the height a seated man's shoulders would be, and Monsieur Albert, an owlbear and a nobleman, who has not been addressed in forty years, says into it:

"Sir. There is a gentleman here who would like a word."

Nothing happens in the room.

In the third mirror, the man at the desk stops. The shoulders go still. For four seconds a room that has been typing for a fortnight does not type.

Then it starts again, and it is faster than it was, and it does not stop for the rest of the night.
check.failure_text:
"No."

The first ungentle syllable in forty years. He composes himself immediately and completely.

"Forgive me. Monsieur — I have spent a very long time learning what it is to be looked at by a room that has decided not to include one, and I would not put a second creature through it on an evening's acquaintance, however much I like you. And I do like you. That is not nothing, from in here."

clue.title: For four seconds, he stopped
clue.text: Addressed by Monsieur Albert into the empty air between the barber's chairs, the man in the mirror stopped typing for four seconds. Then resumed, faster, and did not stop again.

options.text: You have walked through that air. Twice. Tonight.

check.success_text:
Everything old and unhelpful in you arrives at once and it does not arrive with an argument. It arrives with an instruction, and the instruction is: *not again, not through that, go round.*

And it is right, and it is right for a reason it cannot articulate and does not need to, which is that both times you went through the volume of air between the chairs, the temperature was wrong on the far side of it. Not cold. *Later.* You came out of it into a room that had been going on for a few seconds longer than the room you went in from.

The animal noticed both times. The animal has been trying to mention it since Tuesday.
check.failure_text: There is a piece of air between two barbers' chairs and it is a piece of air, and going round it would be an admission, so you do not, and nothing whatever happens, and nothing whatever continues to happen for the rest of the evening.

clue.title: You come out of it a few seconds later
clue.text: Crossing the empty volume between the barber's chairs puts you into a room that has been running a few seconds longer than the one you left. It has happened twice and something in you registered it both times.

he_stopped.text:
"He heard," says Albert, and there is something in the glass that has not been in it all evening, and it is not fear.

"Forty years, monsieur. Forty years of being a feature, and it transpires that the whole apparatus can be interrupted by an owlbear being *polite* at the correct piece of empty air.

I shall be doing that again. I want you to know that. Whatever comes of your business — and something is coming, one hears it, the glass carries — I shall be standing in this shop addressing the space between the chairs every evening at six, and I shall keep doing it, and he will have to keep hearing it.

It is not much of a campaign. It is, however, entirely mine."

glass_opinion.text:
"You have been talking to the mirror," says Albert, from inside it. "About me.

Monsieur. I have lived in that surface for forty years and it has never once been rude to me, and I have never once considered that it might have a view. That is precisely the discourtesy I have spent four decades objecting to, performed by me, upon a pane of glass.

I shall have to think about that. Do not tell Antonio. He will put a cup out for it."

walked_through.text:
"You have gone pale, monsieur, which in this establishment is a considerable achievement, as everything is already the colour of a mirror.

Yes. It is a few seconds later on that side. I have watched patrons cross it for forty years and come out the other side very slightly behind the room, and none of them has ever noticed, and Antonio walks through it forty times a day and is the most punctual man in this parish and has never once been late for anything in his life.

I had assumed it was a property of the shop. It has not previously occurred to me to wonder what is on the other side of a *few seconds*."

the_parish_then.text:
"I should not have said that so plainly. You have gone quiet and I have had forty years of practice at being tactful and I appear to have spent all of it on the weather.

Monsieur — take it as a courtesy rather than an alarm. I remember a town that is not in the record. You are investigating a town that is not in the record. We are, I think, the only two people in this parish who have that in common, and I have been waiting a long time for the second one."
